subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should core `openclaw backup create` accept this native exclude-pattern feature, and if so should `.backupignore` be opt-in and per-asset matching be required before merge?
rationale: The PR changes backup restore and sensitive-file behavior through new CLI/file configuration surfaces, so maintainers need to choose the supported core policy before automation can safely repair the branch.

options.title: Require reworked native excludes
options.body: Keep the feature direction, but require a rebase plus explicit `.backupignore` opt-in, per-asset filtering, streaming-safe validation, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to explicit CLI flags
options.body: Drop auto `.backupignore` and only accept repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` once current-main backup hardening is preserved.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: Close or pause this stale branch and ask for a fresh smaller PR if maintainers do not want to sponsor the broad backup-scope change now.

recommendation.title: Require reworked native excludes
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction, but require a rebase plus explicit `.backupignore` opt-in, per-asset filtering, streaming-safe validation, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup hardening and merge history make this the strongest available owner signal for the backup runtime policy choice.
